books.title: Ganita Manjari: Textbook of Mathematics for Grade 9 (Part I)
books.edition: First Edition, April 2026 (Chaitra 1948) — new NCERT book for the 2026-27 session

books.title: Ganita Manjari: Textbook of Mathematics for Grade 9 (Part II)
books.edition: First Edition, August 2026 (Shravana 1948) — new NCERT book for the 2026-27 session

source.method: chapter titles from the book's Contents page; topics from each chapter PDF's section headings

chapters.title: Orienting Yourself: The Use of Coordinates

topics.title: Introduction: Grid-Based Thinking and Coordinates
objectives: Student can explain how a system of coordinates uses numbers to describe exact locations
Student can describe early uses of grids, such as the street plans of the Sindhu-Sarasvatī Civilisation and the use of latitude and longitude for navigation
visualIdeas: a city street grid with North-South and East-West lines at equal spacing

topics.title: Settling In: Locating Places Using Coordinates
objectives: Student can describe the position of a place relative to a chosen origin using two directions at right angles
Student can give and follow directions on a grid, as Shalini does to guide Reiaan around his new school
visualIdeas: a school campus map on a grid with the gate as origin

topics.title: The 2-D Cartesian Coordinate System
objectives: Student can identify the x-axis, y-axis, origin and the four quadrants
Student can read and plot points with positive and negative coordinates
Student can predict the quadrant of a point from the signs of its coordinates
visualIdeas: a Cartesian plane with points plotted in each quadrant and their coordinates labelled

topics.title: Distance Between Two Points in the 2-D Plane
objectives: Student can find the distance between two points using the Baudhāyana-Pythagoras theorem
Student can show that reflecting a figure in an axis preserves the lengths of its sides
visualIdeas: two points joined by a segment with a right triangle drawn on the grid beneath it

topics.title: Algebraic Expressions: Terms, Variables and Coefficients
objectives: Student can identify the terms, variables, coefficients and constant of an algebraic expression
Student can write an algebraic expression for an everyday situation, such as pens and pencils in boxes
visualIdeas: boxes of pens and pencils with the expression 4x + 5y + 3 built beneath them

topics.title: Linear Polynomials
objectives: Student can define the degree of a polynomial and recognise a linear polynomial
Student can find the value of a linear polynomial for given values of the variables
visualIdeas: a sorting board of expressions: linear and not linear

topics.title: Exploring Linear Patterns
objectives: Student can describe a growing pattern that adds the same number at each stage using a linear expression
Student can use a linear expression to predict a later stage, such as a taxi fare for a given distance
visualIdeas: a growing pattern of square tiles, stages 1 to 4, with a table of tile counts

topics.title: Linear Growth and Linear Decay
objectives: Student can distinguish linear growth from linear decay with real-life examples
Student can model linear decay, such as the value of an item that depreciates by a fixed amount each year
visualIdeas: two bar sequences: one rising by a fixed step, one falling by a fixed step

topics.title: Linear Relationships
objectives: Student can recognise a linear relationship of the form y = ax + b between two quantities
Student can use a linear relationship such as the conversion between Celsius and Fahrenheit
visualIdeas: a thermometer with Celsius and Fahrenheit scales side by side

topics.title: Visualising Linear Relationships
objectives: Student can draw the graph of a linear relationship and see that it is a straight line
Student can relate the slope of the line to the rate at which one quantity changes with the other
visualIdeas: a straight-line graph of y = 2x + 1 with a rise-over-run triangle

topics.title: The Dawn of Mathematics: The Human Need to Count
objectives: Student can describe early evidence of counting, such as tally marks on the Ishango bone
Student can explain how trade and astronomy in India drove the development of numbers
visualIdeas: a bone with notched tally marks beside a merchant’s counting tally

topics.title: The Revolution of Śhūnya: When Nothing Became Something
objectives: Student can explain how the idea of śhūnya moved from philosophy into mathematics as the number zero
Student can state Brahmagupta’s rules for zero and describe the Bakhśhālī manuscript as an early record of zero
visualIdeas: a timeline from śhūnyatā to the Bakhśhālī dot to Brahmagupta’s rules

topics.title: Integers: Expanding the Horizon
objectives: Student can explain how negative numbers arose, for example through Brahmagupta’s ideas of fortunes and debts
Student can apply the rules of arithmetic for integers
visualIdeas: a number line with fortunes to the right and debts to the left of zero

topics.title: Fractions and Rational Numbers
objectives: Student can define a rational number as p/q with integers p, q and q ≠ 0
Student can write a rational number in its lowest terms
visualIdeas: a number line between 0 and 1 divided into halves, thirds and quarters

topics.title: Representation of Rational Numbers on the Number Line
objectives: Student can locate rational numbers on the number line
Student can find the absolute value of a rational number as its distance from zero
visualIdeas: a number line with −3/4 and 5/2 marked and their distances from zero

topics.title: The Density of Rational Numbers
objectives: Student can show that there is a rational number between any two rational numbers
Student can find several rational numbers between two given rational numbers
visualIdeas: a zoom sequence on a number line revealing more and more rationals between two numbers

topics.title: Irrational Numbers and the Proof that √2 is Irrational
objectives: Student can explain what an irrational number is
Student can follow the proof by contradiction that √2 is irrational
visualIdeas: a unit square with its diagonal labelled √2

topics.title: Construction of Lengths Like √2 and √3
objectives: Student can construct lengths such as √2 and √3 using right triangles and a compass
Student can locate such lengths on the number line
visualIdeas: a square-root spiral built from right triangles

topics.title: The Story of Pi (π) and Madhava’s Infinite Series
objectives: Student can explain that π is irrational (proved by Lambert) and describe Āryabhaṭa’s approximation 3.1416
Student can describe Madhava’s infinite series as a way to compute π
visualIdeas: a circle with its circumference unrolled beside its diameter

topics.title: Rational Decimals: Terminating and Repeating
objectives: Student can show that every rational number has a terminating or repeating decimal expansion
Student can predict from the denominator in lowest terms whether a decimal will terminate
Student can convert a repeating decimal into the form p/q
visualIdeas: long division of 1/7 showing the remainders repeating

topics.title: The Magic of Cyclic Numbers
objectives: Student can identify 142857 as the repeating block of the decimal for 1/7
Student can show that multiplying 142857 by 1 to 6 only rotates its digits in a cycle
visualIdeas: a circle of the digits 1-4-2-8-5-7 with multiples of 142857 read around it

topics.title: Irrational Decimals and Real Numbers
objectives: Student can explain that irrational numbers have non-terminating, non-repeating decimal expansions
Student can describe the real numbers as all rational and irrational numbers together
visualIdeas: a nested diagram: natural numbers inside whole numbers inside integers inside rationals, with irrationals completing the reals

topics.title: Visualising Identities
objectives: Student can explain the difference between an equation and an identity
Student can show (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² and (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b² using areas of squares and rectangles
Student can use these identities to square numbers quickly
visualIdeas: a square of side a + b split into a², b² and two ab rectangles

topics.title: Factorisation of Algebraic Expressions Using Identities
objectives: Student can factorise expressions by taking out common factors and recognising perfect squares
Student can use a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b) to factorise
visualIdeas: an expression 25p² + 30pq + 9q² rewritten as (5p + 3q)²

topics.title: More Identities: (a + b + c)²
objectives: Student can derive and use the identity (a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2ab + 2bc + 2ca
Student can use it to compute squares such as 119² mentally
visualIdeas: a square of side a + b + c divided into nine regions

topics.title: Factorisation Using Algebra Tiles
objectives: Student can represent products such as (x + 2)(x + 3) with algebra tiles
Student can arrange tiles for a quadratic expression into a rectangle to find its factors
visualIdeas: algebra tiles arranged as a rectangle for x² + 5x + 6

topics.title: Factorisation Without Using Algebra Tiles
objectives: Student can factorise x² + px + q by finding two numbers a and b with a + b = p and ab = q
Student can extend the method of splitting the middle term to other quadratic expressions
visualIdeas: a split of 5x into 2x + 3x with grouping arrows

topics.title: Finding New Identities: Cubes
objectives: Student can derive (a + b)³ and (a − b)³ and show (a + b)³ with a cube cut into smaller cubes and cuboids
Student can use x³ − y³ = (x − y)(x² + xy + y²) and x³ + y³ + z³ − 3xyz = (x + y + z)(x² + y² + z² − xy − yz − zx)
visualIdeas: a cube of edge a + b split into two cubes and six cuboids

topics.title: Simplifying Rational Expressions
objectives: Student can factorise the numerator and denominator of a rational expression using identities
Student can simplify a rational expression by cancelling common factors, assuming the denominator is non-zero
visualIdeas: a fraction of polynomials with matching factors struck out

chapters.title: I'm Up and Down, and Round and Round

topics.title: Definitions and Symmetries of a Circle
objectives: Student can define a circle, its centre, radius, diameter, chord, arc and segment
Student can describe the reflection and rotation symmetries of a circle
visualIdeas: a labelled circle with radius, diameter, chord and arc
a circle with several lines of symmetry through its centre

topics.title: How Many Circles?
objectives: Student can explain how many circles pass through one point, two points and three points
Student can construct the unique circle through three non-collinear points using perpendicular bisectors
visualIdeas: three non-collinear points with perpendicular bisectors meeting at the circumcentre

topics.title: Chords and the Angles They Subtend
objectives: Student can describe a chord and the angle it subtends at the centre using a thread tied across a wheel
Student can prove that equal chords subtend equal angles at the centre, and the converse
visualIdeas: two equal chords with their central angles shaded

topics.title: Midpoints and Perpendicular Bisectors of Chords
objectives: Student can prove that the perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects it, and the converse
Student can use the result to find a chord length or the distance of a chord from the centre
visualIdeas: a chord with a perpendicular from the centre meeting it at its midpoint

topics.title: Distance of Chords from the Centre
objectives: Student can prove that equal chords are equidistant from the centre, and the converse
Student can decide which of two unequal chords is farther from the centre
visualIdeas: a long chord near the centre and a short chord far from it

topics.title: Angles Subtended by an Arc
objectives: Student can prove that the angle subtended by an arc at the centre is twice the angle at any point on the remaining part of the circle
Student can use the result for angles in the same segment and the angle in a semicircle
visualIdeas: an arc with its central angle and an inscribed angle drawn, the central angle double

topics.title: Concyclicity of Points
objectives: Student can state the condition for four points to be concyclic
Student can prove and use that opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180°
visualIdeas: a cyclic quadrilateral with opposite angles labelled summing to 180°

topics.title: Perimeter of a Shape
objectives: Student can find the perimeter of polygons and composite shapes
Student can explain why runners start at staggered positions on an athletics track
visualIdeas: a 400 m athletics track with staggered starting lines

topics.title: Perimeter of a Circle: The C/D Ratio
objectives: Student can measure the circumference and diameter of round objects and find that C/D is roughly constant
Student can use C = πd and C = 2πr and describe how Archimedes bounded π using polygons
visualIdeas: a circle squeezed between an inscribed and a circumscribed hexagon

topics.title: π (Pi) is Irrational
objectives: Student can explain that π cannot be written as a ratio of two integers and has no repeating pattern in its digits
Student can explain why 22/7 and 355/113 are only approximations of π
visualIdeas: π written to many decimal places beside 22/7 = 3.142857…

topics.title: Length of an Arc of a Circle
objectives: Student can find the length of an arc from its central angle and the radius
Student can apply arc length to the curved parts of a 400 m athletics track
visualIdeas: a sector with the arc highlighted and its angle θ marked

topics.title: Problems, Puzzles, and Paradoxes on Perimeter
objectives: Student can find the perimeter of shapes made of circular arcs, such as two equal circles passing through each other’s centres
Student can show that a path of three small semicircles on a diameter has the same length as the large semicircle on it
visualIdeas: a large semicircle above a line and three smaller semicircles below it joining the same two points

topics.title: Area of a Rectangle and a Parallelogram
objectives: Student can find the area of a rectangle and of a parallelogram as base × height
Student can explain, by cutting and moving a triangle, why a parallelogram has the same area as a rectangle with the same base and height
visualIdeas: a parallelogram with a triangle cut off one end and moved to form a rectangle

topics.title: Area of a Triangle and Heron’s Formula
objectives: Student can find the area of a triangle as ½ × base × height
Student can use Heron’s formula to find the area of a triangle from its three sides
visualIdeas: a triangle with sides a, b, c and its semi-perimeter s

topics.title: Brahmagupta’s Formula for a Cyclic Quadrilateral
objectives: Student can use Brahmagupta’s formula for the area of a cyclic quadrilateral
Student can explain how Heron’s formula is a special case of Brahmagupta’s formula
visualIdeas: a cyclic quadrilateral whose fourth side shrinks to zero to become a triangle

topics.title: Squaring a Rectangle
objectives: Student can explain what it means to square a shape
Student can follow Baudhāyana’s construction from the Śhulba-sūtra to build a square equal in area to a given rectangle
visualIdeas: a rectangle and an equal-area square built from it

topics.title: Area of a Circle and a Sector
objectives: Student can explain the formula πr² for the area of a circle by rearranging sectors
Student can find the area of a sector of a circle
visualIdeas: a circle cut into thin sectors and rearranged into a near-rectangle

chapters.title: The Mathematics of Maybe: Introduction to Probability

topics.title: What is Probability? Randomness and the Probability Scale
objectives: Student can describe random events whose outcomes cannot be predicted with certainty
Student can place events on a probability scale from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain)
visualIdeas: a 0-to-1 scale with impossible, unlikely, even chance, likely and certain marked

topics.title: Experimental Probability
objectives: Student can find experimental probability as the relative frequency of an outcome over many trials
Student can carry out a coin or die experiment and record outcomes
visualIdeas: a tally chart of 50 coin tosses with the fraction of heads

topics.title: Theoretical Probability
objectives: Student can find theoretical probability for equally likely outcomes
Student can compare experimental and theoretical probability as the number of trials grows
visualIdeas: a fair die with each face labelled 1/6

topics.title: Analysing Statistical Data Using Probability
objectives: Student can use data from surveys and records to estimate probabilities
Student can explain the gambler’s fallacy and what makes a coin or die fair and unbiased
visualIdeas: a streak of five heads with a speech bubble asking whether tails is now due

topics.title: Sample Spaces and Events
objectives: Student can list the sample space of an experiment
Student can describe an event as a subset of the sample space and find its probability
visualIdeas: the sample space of rolling a die with an event circled

topics.title: Tree Diagrams
objectives: Student can draw a tree diagram to list the outcomes of an experiment done in stages
Student can use a tree diagram to find probabilities, such as for tossing two coins
visualIdeas: a two-level tree diagram for tossing two coins

chapters.title: Predicting What Comes Next: Exploring Sequences and Progressions

topics.title: Introduction to Sequences
objectives: Student can recognise sequences and their terms, such as square and triangular numbers
Student can predict the next terms of a sequence from its pattern
visualIdeas: dot patterns for triangular and square numbers

topics.title: Explicit Rule for a Sequence
objectives: Student can write the nth term of a sequence as an explicit rule
Student can find any term of a sequence from its explicit rule
visualIdeas: a table of n and the nth term with an arrow to the formula

topics.title: Recursive Rule for a Sequence
objectives: Student can write a recursive rule that gives each term from the previous terms
Student can generate the Virahāṅka-Fibonacci sequence from its recursive rule
visualIdeas: a chain of terms where each term is the sum of the two before it

topics.title: Arithmetic Progressions
objectives: Student can identify an arithmetic progression and its common difference
Student can find the nth term of an AP and visualise it as points on a straight line
visualIdeas: an AP shown as equally spaced bars rising by the same step

topics.title: Sum of the First n Natural Numbers
objectives: Student can find 1 + 2 + … + n = n(n + 1)/2 by pairing terms
Student can use this to find the sum of terms of an AP
visualIdeas: a staircase of blocks doubled to form a rectangle n by n + 1

topics.title: Geometric Progressions
objectives: Student can identify a geometric progression and its common ratio
Student can find the nth term of a GP
visualIdeas: a sequence of squares doubling in number at each step

topics.title: Fun with Fractals and Visualising a GP
objectives: Student can describe fractals such as the snowflake built by repeating a rule, and see GPs in them
Student can visualise the terms of a GP with diagrams
visualIdeas: the first three stages of a snowflake fractal

topics.title: Propositions and their Converses
objectives: Student can define a proposition as a statement that is either true or false
Student can write the converse of a proposition of the form ‘if X then Y’, also expressed as ‘X implies Y’ or ‘Y when X’
visualIdeas: two arrows: X → Y for the proposition and Y → X for its converse

topics.title: Counterexamples
objectives: Student can explain how a single counterexample shows that a proposition is false
Student can find counterexamples, such as for “if a number is a multiple of 3, then it is a multiple of 6”
Student can describe how Euler disproved Fermat’s claim about numbers of the form 2^(2^n) + 1
visualIdeas: a wet road with a tanker, as a counterexample to “if the road is wet, it has rained”

topics.title: When Both a Proposition and its Converse are True
objectives: Student can show that a number is a perfect square exactly when it has an odd number of factors
Student can prove the converse of the Baudhāyana-Pythagoras theorem using SSS congruence
Student can give examples where a proposition is true but its converse is false
visualIdeas: factor-partner pairs of 36 with the repeated pair (6, 6) highlighted

topics.title: Average of Averages
objectives: Student can explain why the average of two group averages is not always the average of the whole group
Student can find the correct combined average using group sizes
visualIdeas: two groups of different sizes with their averages and the combined average

topics.title: Mixtures
objectives: Student can find the concentration of a mixture, such as lemonade with different amounts of jaggery
Student can explain why the concentration of a mixture is a simple average only when equal quantities are mixed
visualIdeas: two jugs of different strengths poured into one

topics.title: Custom Weights: Weighted Average
objectives: Student can compute a weighted average when items carry different weights
Student can apply weighted averages to marks and other real situations
visualIdeas: a balance beam with values placed at weighted positions

topics.title: Stacking Columns: Stacked Bar Charts
objectives: Student can read and draw stacked bar charts
Student can compare totals and parts across categories using a stacked bar chart
visualIdeas: a stacked bar chart of family expenditure split into food, housing, healthcare and recreation

topics.title: An Alternative to Pie Charts: 100% Stacked Bar Charts
objectives: Student can draw a 100% stacked bar chart to compare shares across groups
Student can choose between pie charts and 100% stacked bars to answer a question
Student can draw inferences from data such as a typical day’s time use
visualIdeas: three pie charts beside one 100% stacked bar chart of the same data

topics.title: Adding Numbers Digit by Digit
objectives: Student can describe an algorithm as a precise, step-by-step procedure
Student can write the column-addition method with carries as an algorithm
visualIdeas: column addition with carry digits highlighted step by step

topics.title: Greatest Common Divisor: Divisors and a First Algorithm
objectives: Student can list the divisors of a number systematically
Student can write an algorithm to find the gcd by listing divisors
visualIdeas: two lists of divisors with the common ones circled and the greatest starred

topics.title: Data Structures: Lists and Improving the Algorithm
objectives: Student can explain how a list is used to store data in an algorithm
Student can improve the gcd algorithm by computing common divisors directly and doing away with lists
Student can compare algorithms by the number of steps they take
visualIdeas: three versions of the gcd algorithm side by side with their step counts

topics.title: Euclid’s Subtraction Algorithm
objectives: Student can find the gcd by repeatedly subtracting the smaller number from the larger
Student can explain the idea of reducing a problem to a simpler one
visualIdeas: a pair of numbers shrinking step by step as the smaller is subtracted from the larger

topics.title: Āryabhaṭa’s Division Algorithm
objectives: Student can find the gcd using repeated division with remainders
Student can explain why the division algorithm takes fewer steps than repeated subtraction
visualIdeas: a ladder of divisions with remainders shrinking to zero

topics.title: What Exactly is a Quadrilateral?
objectives: Student can define a quadrilateral and distinguish convex from non-convex quadrilaterals
Student can show that the angles of a quadrilateral add up to 360°
visualIdeas: a convex and a non-convex quadrilateral with their diagonals drawn

topics.title: Parallelograms
objectives: Student can prove the properties of a parallelogram: opposite sides equal, opposite angles equal and diagonals bisecting each other
Student can use the conditions that make a quadrilateral a parallelogram
Student can relate rectangles, rhombuses and squares as special parallelograms
visualIdeas: a parallelogram with equal sides, equal angles and bisecting diagonals marked

topics.title: An Important Property of Triangles: The Midpoint Theorem
objectives: Student can prove that the segment joining the midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half its length
Student can show that joining the midpoints of the sides of any quadrilateral gives a parallelogram (Varignon)
visualIdeas: a triangle with its midpoint segment drawn parallel to the base

topics.title: A Surprising Property of Medians
objectives: Student can show that the three medians of a triangle meet at one point, the centroid
Student can state that the centroid divides each median in the ratio 2 : 1
visualIdeas: a triangle with three medians meeting at the centroid

topics.title: Tiling the Plane Using Any 4-gon
objectives: Student can explain why copies of any quadrilateral can tile the plane
Student can describe the recent discovery of an aperiodic tile
visualIdeas: a plane tiled with copies of an irregular quadrilateral

topics.title: Linear Equations in Two Variables and their Standard Form
objectives: Student can write a situation as a linear equation in two variables
Student can write a linear equation in the standard form ax + by + c = 0
visualIdeas: a word problem turned into ax + by + c = 0

topics.title: Solutions of a Linear Equation in Two Variables
objectives: Student can check whether an ordered pair is a solution of a linear equation
Student can explain that a linear equation in two variables has infinitely many solutions that lie on a straight line
visualIdeas: a line on a grid with several solution points marked

topics.title: Understanding Slope
objectives: Student can find the slope of a line as rise over run
Student can relate steepness and direction of a line to its slope
visualIdeas: three lines of different steepness with their rise-run triangles

topics.title: Slope-Intercept Form
objectives: Student can write a linear equation in the form y = mx + c and read the slope and y-intercept
Student can draw a line from its slope and y-intercept
visualIdeas: a line crossing the y-axis at c with slope m marked

topics.title: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
objectives: Student can form a pair of linear equations from a word problem
Student can explain what a solution of a pair of linear equations means
visualIdeas: two lines on one grid crossing at a point

topics.title: Algebraic Methods: Substitution and Elimination
objectives: Student can solve a pair of linear equations by substitution
Student can solve a pair of linear equations by elimination
visualIdeas: two equations stacked with one variable eliminated

topics.title: Graphical Method for Solving a Pair of Linear Equations
objectives: Student can solve a pair of linear equations by drawing their graphs
Student can relate intersecting, parallel and coincident lines to a unique solution, no solution and infinitely many solutions
visualIdeas: three small graphs: intersecting, parallel and coincident lines

chapters.title: Math of Space: Surface Area and Volume

topics.title: Cuboids and Cubes
objectives: Student can find the lateral and total surface area of cuboids and cubes using their nets
Student can find the volume of cuboids and cubes
visualIdeas: a cuboid unfolded into its net with face areas labelled

topics.title: Right Circular Cylinder
objectives: Student can find the curved and total surface area of a cylinder using its net
Student can find the volume of a cylinder
visualIdeas: a cylinder unrolled into a rectangle and two circles

topics.title: Cones
objectives: Student can find the slant height, curved surface area and total surface area of a cone
Student can find the volume of a cone as one-third of the cylinder with the same base and height
visualIdeas: a cone and a cylinder of the same base and height, the cylinder filled by three cones

topics.title: Pyramidal Shapes
objectives: Student can describe a pyramidal shape by its base and apex and give examples such as the pyramids of Egypt
Student can find the volume of a pyramid as one-third of base area × height and relate it to the volume of a cone
visualIdeas: a square pyramid with its net

topics.title: Spheres and Hemispheres
objectives: Student can find the surface area of a sphere and verify the formula with the hands-on string activity
Student can find the volume of a sphere and the surface area and volume of a hemisphere
visualIdeas: a ball wound with string, and the same string filling four circles of the same radius

topics.title: Areas and Volumes Around Us: Guesstimates
objectives: Student can make reasonable guesstimates of areas and volumes of everyday objects
Student can apply surface area and volume formulas to real-life problems
visualIdeas: a water tank with a question about how many litres it holds
